summary: Enhance your NGO's efficiency with our Agile Project Management training course. Learn essential skills to adapt and thrive in dynamic environments.
lede: Agile Project Management for NGOs helps programme teams plan, deliver, monitor, and improve development, humanitarian, advocacy, and community programmes through short feedback cycles. It combines Agile values with Scrum, Kanban, Results-Based Management, and Theory of Change so teams can respond to changing funding conditions, community needs, partner constraints, and fixed reporting deadlines while keeping evidence visible. Through hands-on practice, you will turn outcomes and logical frameworks into user stories and a prioritized backlog, set sprint goals, coordinate partners, review evidence, manage risks, and report progress against indicators. You will also create practical delivery and governance artefacts, including stakeholder maps, risk registers, monitoring dashboards, change-control records, and donor progress reports, while keeping safeguarding controls and grant commitments in view.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate NGO programmes, grants, field delivery, monitoring, partnerships, and organizational accountability. It suits experienced practitioners who need a structured way to adapt plans without losing donor evidence or community focus.
prerequisites: You should have practical experience supporting or managing an NGO, humanitarian, development, advocacy, or community programme. Familiarity with workplans, logical frameworks, budgets, donor reporting, or monitoring indicators will help you gain more from the exercises. No coding or programming is required. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted evidence analysis, portfolio governance, and PRINCE2 Agile are covered at conceptual and operational application levels, while backlog design, sprint planning, Kanban workflow, risk review, and reporting receive hands-on practice.
